original_question: A 46-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of diplopia and ocular pain when reading the newspaper. She also has a 3-month history of amenorrhea, hot flashes, and increased sweating. She reports that she has been overweight all her adult life and is happy to have lost 6.8-kg (15-lb) of weight in the past 2 months. Her pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 148/98 mm Hg. Physical examination shows moist palms and a nontender thyroid gland that is enlarged to two times its normal size. Ophthalmologic examination shows prominence of the globes of the eyes, bilateral lid retraction, conjunctival injection, and an inability to converge the eyes. There is no pain on movement of the extraocular muscles. Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally. Neurologic examination shows a fine resting tremor of the hands. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ with a shortened relaxation phase. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's ocular complaints?

base.stage_1: A 46-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of double vision and eye pain that worsens when reading. She also reports a cessation of menses for the past 3 months, accompanied by hot flashes and increased sweating.
base.stage_2: The patient's pulse is 110/min and blood pressure is 148/98 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals moist palms and a diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid gland. Ophthalmologic examination demonstrates proptosis, bilateral lid retraction, conjunctival injection, and impaired convergence. There is no pain with extraocular movements. Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally. Neurologic examination reveals a fine resting tremor of the hands and 3+ deep tendon reflexes with a shortened relaxation phase.
base.stage_3: Laboratory studies reveal a suppressed TSH and elevated free T4. An MRI of the orbits shows enlargement of the extraocular muscles, particularly the inferior and medial rectus muscles, with sparing of the tendons.
base.stage_4: An orbital biopsy reveals infiltration of orbital tissues with lymphocytes and increased deposition of glycosaminoglycans.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The absence of proptosis and lid retraction argues against glycosaminoglycan accumulation in the orbit, which typically causes these findings due to orbital tissue expansion.
